title: A Szemerédi-Trotter Theorem in Arbitrary Fields
summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p\ge0$. We prove that $m$ points and $n$ lines in $k^2$ determine at most $3(mn)^{2/3}+m+n+2mn/p$ incidences, the last term being omitted in characteristic zero. Over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$ the coefficient of $mn/p$ can be replaced by $1$. The proof uses the polynomial method, and for $m=n$ the bound is sharp up to an absolute constant over prime fields.
